newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices mixed, supported by cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices mixed, supported by cold.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices surged early Thursday on cold Midwest weather but then declined as buyers stepped away from the market and a Gulf line was expected to resume normal service Friday, sources said.

Gulf Coast prices soared into the $2.50s early on Transco (Station 65), but as buyers for both heating and storage demand disappeared prices fell to as low as the high-$2.20s. Some late shortcovering helped to boost prices slightly shortly before nomination deadlines, traders said.
Tennessee Gas said Wednesday its Louisiana 500 line, shut Tuesday due to a gas leak, would be back to normal Friday.
The Tennessee outage affected about 250 million cubic feet per day from secondary service upstream of station 823 (Kinder).
The short supply available to the west kept south Texas prices strong as traders reported closing most deals in the mid-$2.30s.
This shortage, coupled with expensive Canadian gas, helped prop up southern California border prices further. For delivery through the weekend, prices gained about five cents to the mid-$2.30s.
Similary in the Permian basin, prices were up an average of five cents to the low-$2.30s, though deals were reported done anywhere from the low-$2.20s to $2.35.
At Waha, early deals were done in the high-$2.30s, but as trading progressed prices slipped into the low-$2.30s.
In the Midcontinent, well below-normal temperatures pushed prices three to five cents higher into the high-$2.20s to mid-$2.30s, with the lower-priced deals surfacing late.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to dip to levels 10 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit below normal on Friday but then begin to moderate by Sunday.
At the New York city-gate, where temperatures are expected to drop to below-normal levels this weekend, prices gained several cents to the mid-$2.70s to low-$2.80s.
